*Camera Jabber* | 18/08/2026 | Score: 0.98
Tags: photography, camera, lens

> Here is something you do not see often: a camera manufacturer asking the public which lenses it should build. Fujifilm has hosted a live “Focus on Glass” event on YouTube, putting forward 14 lens concepts and inviting photographers to vote on which should become reality. Three will be chosen. Details are on Fujifilm’s site, with the event on Fujifilm’s YouTube channel. It is a smart piece of engagement, and more than a marketing gesture. Lens development is expensive and slow, and manufacturers routinely misjudge what photographers actually want — the gap between the lenses that get made and the lenses people ask for on forums is a long-running frustration in this industry. Putting 14 concepts in front of the people who would buy them is a reasonable way to close it. There is a hard-headed commercial logic too.
